table.name: Addresses
table.purpose: Postal addresses for students (permanent and current), part of a university enrollment database. One row per address, referenced by Students.permanent_address_id and Students.current_address_id. Data appears to be synthetic/fake (fictional cities, mismatched countries and US states).

address_id.name: address_id
address_id.description: Primary key, surrogate identifier for each address row.

city.name: city
city.description: City name of the address. Values are fictional/synthetic city names (e.g. 'Goodwinhaven', 'Lake Laishafurt').

country.name: country
country.description: Country of the address. Real country names, but randomly generated (inconsistent with the US state values in state_province_county), so likely synthetic data.

line_1.name: line_1
line_1.description: First address line: street number, street name, and optionally unit designator (e.g. '0144 Lamar Plaza Apt. 346').

state_province_county.name: state_province_county
state_province_county.description: State/province/county of the address. Values are US state names (some concatenated without spaces, e.g. 'SouthDakota'), inconsistent with the country values — synthetic data.

zip_postcode.name: zip_postcode
zip_postcode.description: ZIP/postal code, stored as text. Values are 3-digit numeric strings (e.g. '068', '943'), clearly synthetic rather than real postal codes.

table.name: Courses
table.purpose: Catalog of courses offered; each row is one course, identified by course_id, with a short name and description. Referenced by Sections and Student_Enrolment_Courses, so it is the master course list for scheduling and enrolment. The data appears to be anonymized/synthetic (single-letter descriptions, abbreviated names).

course_description.name: course_description
course_description.description: Free-text description of the course. Values are single letters (q, l, p, v, b, ...), suggesting anonymized or placeholder data rather than real descriptions.

course_id.name: course_id
course_id.description: Primary key of the Courses table; unique integer identifying each course (1-15). Referenced by Sections.course_id and Student_Enrolment_Courses.course_id.

course_name.name: course_name
course_name.description: Short name/title of the course. Values are abbreviations of academic subjects (math, cal = calculus, db = databases, dl = deep learning, ds = data structures, os = operating systems, nlp, la = linear algebra, fr = French, en = English, ai).

table.name: Degree_Programs
table.purpose: Catalog of degree programs offered by the university; each row is one degree program (Bachelor, Master, or PhD) belonging to a department, which students enrol into via Student_Enrolment.

degree_program_id.name: degree_program_id
degree_program_id.description: Primary key uniquely identifying each degree program; referenced by Student_Enrolment.degree_program_id.

degree_summary_description.name: degree_summary_description
degree_summary_description.description: Text description of the degree program. Values are placeholder/lorem-ipsum words (e.g. 'aperiam', 'architecto'), so the intended semantic content cannot be verified beyond being a free-text description.

degree_summary_name.name: degree_summary_name
degree_summary_name.description: Degree level of the program: Bachelor, Master, or PHD.

department_id.name: department_id
department_id.description: Foreign key to Departments.department_id; the department that offers the degree program.

table.name: Departments
table.purpose: Lookup table of academic departments at an institution; each row is one department. Referenced by Degree_Programs via department_id. Descriptions are placeholder (lorem-ipsum-like) filler text, so they carry no real semantic content.

department_description.name: department_description
department_description.description: Free-text description of the department. Values are Latin filler words (e.g. 'consequatur', 'nihil'), suggesting placeholder/test data rather than real descriptions.

department_id.name: department_id
department_id.description: Primary key of the Departments table; unique integer identifier for each department (1-15). Referenced by Degree_Programs.department_id.

department_name.name: department_name
department_name.description: Name of the department (e.g. 'art', 'biology', 'computer science', 'math'). Unique across rows.

table.name: Sections
table.purpose: One row per course section (offering) of a course; each section belongs to a course and has a short name/label and a description. Likely referenced by enrolment/transcript tables to identify which section a student took.

course_id.name: course_id
course_id.description: Identifier of the course this section belongs to; references Courses.course_id (many sections to one course).

section_description.name: section_description
section_description.description: Free-text description of the section (values are placeholder lorem-ipsum words, so only the column's descriptive role is supported).

section_id.name: section_id
section_id.description: Primary key; unique numeric identifier of the section.

section_name.name: section_name
section_name.description: Short unique label for the section, one letter per section (a, b, c, ...), i.e. the section letter within a course.

table.name: Semesters
table.purpose: Lookup table of academic semesters/terms (e.g. spring 2010, summer 2010, winter 2010), referenced by student enrolment records. One row per semester.

semester_id.name: semester_id
semester_id.description: Primary key; unique integer identifier (1-15) for each semester. Referenced by Student_Enrolment.semester_id.

semester_name.name: semester_name
semester_name.description: Human-readable semester name in the form '<term> <year>' (e.g. spring 2018, summer 2010, winter 2010). Nearly unique; 'spring 2018' appears twice, suggesting it may not be a strict key.

table.name: Student_Enrolment
table.purpose: One row per enrolment record: a student enrolled in a degree program in a specific semester. Courses taken under an enrolment are linked via Student_Enrolment_Courses.

degree_program_id.name: degree_program_id
degree_program_id.description: References Degree_Programs.degree_program_id; the degree program in which the student is enrolled for this enrolment.

semester_id.name: semester_id
semester_id.description: References Semesters.semester_id; the semester in which the enrolment takes place.

student_enrolment_id.name: student_enrolment_id
student_enrolment_id.description: Primary key of the table; unique identifier of the enrolment. Referenced by Student_Enrolment_Courses to attach courses to the enrolment.

student_id.name: student_id
student_id.description: References Students.student_id; the student who is enrolled.

table.name: Student_Enrolment_Courses
table.purpose: Junction/association table linking a student's enrolment record to the specific courses taken; each row is one course within a student's enrolment, identified by a unique student_course_id that is later referenced by transcript contents.

course_id.name: course_id
course_id.description: Identifier of the course taken, referencing Courses.course_id (many-to-one). Values are small integers (2-14) matching course records with descriptions.

student_course_id.name: student_course_id
student_course_id.description: Primary key of this table: unique identifier for one course within a student's enrolment. Referenced by Transcript_Contents.student_course_id, so it is the link between an enrolment course and its transcript entry. Value distribution is mixed (small integers and large 8-digit values), suggesting rows from different sources or seed data, but its uniqueness and reference support this meaning.

student_enrolment_id.name: student_enrolment_id
student_enrolment_id.description: Identifier of the student's enrolment record, referencing Student_Enrolment.student_enrolment_id (many-to-one). Several courses can belong to the same enrolment.

table.name: Students
table.purpose: One row per student: personal identity and contact details, registration dates, and links to current and permanent addresses. Referenced by Student_Enrolment for enrolment records.

cell_mobile_number.name: cell_mobile_number
cell_mobile_number.description: Student's mobile phone number, stored in inconsistent formats (various punctuation and optional extensions).

current_address_id.name: current_address_id
current_address_id.description: Foreign key to Addresses.address_id; the student's current (term-time) address.

date_first_registered.name: date_first_registered
date_first_registered.description: Timestamp when the student first registered at the institution. Note: values span 1971-2018, which is implausibly early for real registrations, suggesting synthetic/random data.

date_left.name: date_left
date_left.description: Timestamp when the student left the institution. Note: values are not consistently after date_first_registered (e.g. row 7 registered 2018 but left 1997), so the data appears synthetic or corrupted; the intended meaning is likely the date the student left/graduated.

email_address.name: email_address
email_address.description: Student's email address; unique per row, example-domain placeholder values.

permanent_address_id.name: permanent_address_id
permanent_address_id.description: Foreign key to Addresses.address_id; the student's permanent (home) address.

ssn.name: ssn
ssn.description: Intended as the student's Social Security Number, but values are inconsistent (empty strings, 2-3 digit numbers, one 9-digit value), so it does not hold valid SSNs; likely a corrupted or synthetic identifier field.

student_id.name: student_id
student_id.description: Primary key of the Students table; unique surrogate identifier for each student, referenced by Student_Enrolment.student_id.

table.name: Transcript_Contents
table.purpose: Junction table linking transcripts to the individual student-course enrolments they contain; each row states that a given enrolled course appears on a given student's transcript.

student_course_id.name: student_course_id
student_course_id.description: Identifier of a student's enrolment in a specific course (references Student_Enrolment_Courses.student_course_id, many-to-one). The value 0 appears repeatedly and may be a placeholder/unknown, but the evidence is insufficient to confirm this.

transcript_id.name: transcript_id
transcript_id.description: Identifier of the transcript (references Transcripts.transcript_id, many-to-one) on which the referenced course enrolment is listed.

table.name: Transcripts
table.purpose: One row per academic transcript issued to a student; the transcript's line items (courses/grades) live in Transcript_Contents, which references this table via transcript_id. Likely links to students through Transcript_Contents or Student_Enrolment, though no direct join was detected.

transcript_date.name: transcript_date
transcript_date.description: Timestamp when the transcript was issued/generated. Stored as VARCHAR but values parse as datetimes ranging from 1975 to 2013; all 15 values are distinct. The wide, seemingly random range suggests synthetic or seeded data, but the column's meaning as the transcript date is clear.

transcript_id.name: transcript_id
transcript_id.description: Primary key of the Transcripts table; surrogate integer identifier (1-15, all unique). Referenced by Transcript_Contents.transcript_id, which holds the per-course entries of each transcript.
